title: Oversubscription signal-blend causes burst avalanche and tenant request shedding
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: During a staged rollout of the new 'signal-blend' heuristic for headroom prediction, several dedicated reserved pools in us-west experienced rapid oversubscription followed by burst-limit exhaustion and customer request shedding. Affected tenants observed elevated 429/503 errors for burst traffic and an increase in tail latency for short chat requests. We received escalations from three customers (Zeno Analytics, MediLoop, and Finora) and opened emergency pages.

Root cause: A change in how signal-blend weighs short-term burst signals versus long-term utilization introduced a regression when two signals arrived near-simultaneously. The autoscaler pipeline (signal aggregation -> predictor -> lease allocator) applied the new blending factor asynchronously; under a high-cardinality tenant mix this produced an overestimation of available headroom for several pools. The allocator attempted to commit burst reservations against depleted burst-credit ledgers, triggering cascading evictions and a fast-feedback oversubscription loop. The immediate catalyst was a canary rollout of signal-blend + a coincident traffic microburst from several customers.

Why this was missed: Canary guardrails checked for aggregate latency and total reserved capacity changes but did not validate transient blend-weighted headroom estimates or run end-to-end leakage checks for burst-credit accounting. Unit-level tests for the new blend logic passed, but integration tests and telemetry coverage for the blend-to-allocator path were insufficient.

Impact: Short-lived but severe: 10-45 minute windows of degraded service for affected tenants across 3 clusters; some customers experienced failed inference requests and increased error budgets. Financial exposure: potential SLA credits for 3 enterprise customers.

Immediate remediation performed:
- Rolled back the signal-blend rollout to previous stable weighting (completed 2026-03-10 15:12 UTC).
- Repaired burst-credit ledgers by running the ledger reconciliation job (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/11487).
- Manually injected emergency reserved capacity to impacted pools and throttled low-priority background warmups to free headroom (playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/dedicated-emergency-runbook).
- Deployed a scoped hotfix preventing allocator from committing reservations when ledger variance > 20% (hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/577).

Current status: Hotfix merged, stepped canary of a conservative blend variant scheduled. PRs for ledger reconciliation and allocator guardrails are under review. Incident declared and postmortem meeting scheduled.

RCA summary: Missing integration tests and insufficient telemetry on blended headroom; asynchronous application of blend factor created transient over-optimistic headroom; allocator lacked sufficient defensive checks for ledger variance.

Longer-term mitigation plan (high level):
1) Telemetry: add a headroom-estimate histogram and a signal-delta trace for the blend pipeline; emit a per-pool 'blend-variance' signal to alert on divergence.
2) Safety checks: prevent allocator commits when blend variance or ledger discrepancy exceeds thresholds; add fallback path to use conservative predictor when confidence is low.
3) Testing: add end-to-end injections in CI that simulate high-cardinality mixes and overlapping microbursts; add chaos tests that assert no burst-credit double-commit.
4) Runbook: expand canary gating to include blended-headroom and ledger reconciliation sanity checks; automate emergency capacity uplift for impacted pools.
5) Communication: customer-facing incident report, SLA remediation, and dedicated follow-up sessions with the three affected customers.

Artifacts:
- Grafana incident dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/alerts/dedicated-oversubscription-2026-03
- Allocator hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/577
- Ledger reconciliation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/11487
- Canary gating doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/signal-blend-canary

action_items: Add blend-variance metric to telemetry and alert when > 15% for > 1m
Add allocator guardrail to reject commits when ledger variance > 20%
Implement CI E2E injection test for high-cardinality microbursts
Expand canary gating to include blended-headroom and ledger sanity checks
Run a 72-hour soak with conservative blend weighting in staging and perf clusters
Document incident and customer remediation steps; schedule 1:1s with impacted customers
